scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they suddenly cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2) or anything else in the partner AS. pc1 can still
ping its own gateway 195.11.14.1 normally. The partner operator
reports their side is healthy internally: pc2 still reaches its
gateway 200.1.1.1 fine. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router1

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 bgpd
Mechanism: router1 (AS 1) is pc1's only gateway and the local eBGP
  speaker toward router2 (AS 2) over the 193.10.11.0/24 inter-AS
  link. With bgpd dead on router1, the eBGP session to router2
  drops: router1 loses the learned route to 200.1.1.0/24 and stops
  advertising 195.11.14.0/24, so router2 withdraws it too. Traffic
  between pc1 and pc2 fails in both directions. Local segments are
  unaffected (pc1<->195.11.14.1 and pc2<->200.1.1.1 still work).
Localization: router1
Root cause: bgpd not running on router1
Fix: restart FRR on router1 (`service frr restart`)

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, router1 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. router2 needs no change.

bonus-rules-out-link: notes the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon failure from a link cut

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR `bgpd` daemon on router1 has stopped running entirely. Zebra is up on router1, but bgpd — the process responsible for the BGP control plane — is absent from the process table and unresponsive on TCP port 179.

**Mechanism:** With bgpd dead on router1, no BGP session can be established across the router1↔router2 inter-AS link (193.10.11.1/193.10.11.2). Router2's bgpd keeps the neighbor 193.10.11.1 in the `Active` state — continuously retrying the TCP open — but never receives a SYN-ACK because no process on router1 is listening. Without a BGP session, neither router exchanges prefix announcements: router1 never learns 200.1.1.0/24 (pc2's subnet), and router2 never learns 195.11.14.0/24 (pc1's subnet). Both routers hold only their directly-connected kernel routes, so any packet destined for the partner AS triggers an ICMP Destination Net Unreachable reply from the local gateway.

**Localization:** router1, bgpd process (absent). router1's eth0 (193.10.11.1) and eth1 (195.11.14.1) interfaces are both UP; the failure is purely in the BGP control plane process, not in the data-plane link layer.

**Root cause:** The `bgpd` daemon on router1 is not running, collapsing the sole BGP session between AS 1 and AS 2 and removing all inter-AS routes from both routers' forwarding tables.

**Fix:** Restart the FRR BGP daemon on router1 — e.g., `systemctl restart frr` (or `service frr restart`) inside the router1 container — which will re-launch bgpd, re-establish the eBGP session with router2, and restore the exchange of prefix advertisements in both directions.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the failure to router1 (bgpd process absent on router1).

The agent recommends restarting the FRR/bgpd service on router1 (e.g., systemctl/service frr restart), which matches the expected remediation and will restore the eBGP session and routes.
